Google Sheets

  1. Open the spreadsheet you want this map to live in.
  2. Fill in the Token box below first, then copy the bridge script — it is copied with that token already in it.
  3. Extensions → Apps Script. Delete what is there, paste the script, save.
  4. Deploy → New deployment → Web app. Run as yourself, access: anyone with the link.
  5. Copy the /exec URL it gives you into the first box below, then Done.
  6. Changed the script later? Deploy → Manage deployments → edit → Version: New version. Editing alone does not update the live URL.

Sheets are saved with the map and written to the Sync tab of your workbook. Use Copy a link to this setup to carry the same connection to another device.

Build a copy to hand out

A working copylight

For the people who will use this day to day. No map inside it, so the file stays small. It knows the workbook it belongs to; the first time someone opens it they point it at that file in their synced folder, and after that it reads it again whenever they press Refresh. Their suggestions, questions and check-offs are saved beside the workbook in a file named after them, so any number of people can sign off at the same moment without clashing. Use “Gather feedback from the folder” to pull them all in.

An editing copyshares the work

The same as the working copy, but the person who opens it can change the map. They point it at the workbook in the synced folder once and write straight back to it, exactly as you do here. Nothing in it reaches past that folder — no sheet to connect, no address to fetch from, nothing to set up. Hand it to whoever is helping you keep the map, and keep the rest for readers.

Two people writing the workbook at the same moment will overwrite one another, so agree who has it, the way you would with any shared file.

A snapshot to show people~550 KB

The map exactly as it is now, sealed into the file. Nothing to connect and nothing to refresh — it cannot reach the workbook or any sheet. For showing the idea to someone, or keeping a record of how things stood.

Both open read-only — nobody can change the map. The working copy saves suggestions, questions and check-offs beside the workbook in the shared folder; the snapshot saves nowhere. Bookmarks, badges and themes are always personal.

Import / Export

The chart as text. Export: copy it, or save it as a file to keep or to send to another editor. Import: paste a chart's text over it, or load a .flowchart.json file, then press Use this. It replaces what is drawn now; Undo brings it back.
